campaign: One idea holds ten films: X0 Bot is a someone, not a screen. Having a team was once the luxury of the man with a secretary, a booking clerk and a switchboard; now it is anyone with a phone, and the team has manners: it does the finding, the writing, the remembering and the shipping, then stops, looks at you, and waits for your yes. Every film is a person's life on real footage (what they SAY is handwriting on their word times), interrupted by paper (what the bots DID arrives taped on, in type), closed by a two-line headline with one handwritten word and one brush underline, and sealed by the same end card. The ten run as a funnel. Awareness: He had a team (the idea, through torn paper onto old films), Pahunch gaye? (the India heart: love as logistics, now opening on a scooter so the train belongs to Plan's film), Great at One Thing (the roster, with the first glimpse of a bot you make yourself). Consideration: Khaana khaya? (Keybot, Hinglish first; Keybot writes, she sends), Leave at 4:40 (Plan: the train arrives as she reaches it), The Hold (Travel, four held things and the pause before pay), Go Live (Code bot, rebuilt as its own shape: hands lift off a keyboard, two holds, the room stands before the rocket goes; it shares only the wait, the written yes and the stamp with The Hold), In One Sentence (make your own bot; the new head takes the centre seat the roster left open). Trust: Uncle is right (India's sceptic wins and we agree), The Witness (the deposition: they ask first, data not for sale). Count-In's hero sweep is the hinge of Great at One Thing; Talk Messy's punctuation thuds and kept-name underline live in Khaana khaya?. The Hold and Go Live are siblings in sea and moss by device, not by cut; Uncle is right and The Witness are the fox's two appearances, split by market. Cut-downs the builders make from these assets: Who Presses Pay (15 s, from The Witness: Q 'And who presses pay?' on black, the fox's hold, his extra recorded line 'You do', black, 'You do' / 'always' in white with a clay underline under 'always', end card) and Face Down (6 s: the phone face down at morning, sourced in the footage list, into the end card). Every line of type in every film is measured against the system's character limits and safe area before paper is drawn.

spots.title: He had a team
spots.director: The Trickster (Jonze, Gondry): paper worlds inside real ones; the painted bot wandering into other people's footage; one in-camera trick that explains the product better than a sentence.
spots.job: Awareness, manifesto, global: the whole idea (a team, each great at one thing, now for anyone).
spots.logline: Through a hole torn in white paper we watch old films of the office that once ran one man's life; a painted bot hangs in every room and a card names the bot that does that job now. He had a team. Now you do.
spots.insight: Having someone was always the luxury. The person with a team got their life back while everyone else carried their day in their head. People do not want a smarter phone; they want a someone.

spots.title: Pahunch gaye?
spots.director: The Humanist (Zoya Akhtar, Ray): everyday India, Hinglish as spoken, the small observed gesture, dignity first.
spots.job: Awareness, India first: love as logistics; Plan and Travel shown in passing.
spots.logline: Every Indian journey ends with the same two-word message. A film of arrivals, one question written over each, and two paper cards that quietly show who got them there.
spots.insight: In India, 'I love you' is sent as 'Pahunch gaye?' The family runs on arrivals and someone is always waiting for the haan. A team that handles leaving-times and tickets is, in the end, in the business of letting you say yes.

spots.title: Great at One Thing
spots.director: The Symmetrist: every frame centred and level, mounted on white paper with a dip-pen rule; tags; a dry narrator; the joke is the point.
spots.job: Awareness: the roster, each bot by colour and verb, and the first sight of a bot you make yourself.
spots.logline: A deadpan census of people great at one thing ends on a man great at dinner and less great at everything after it; the bot swings in, sweeps the rest off the page, and the team takes it.
spots.insight: Nobody is great at everything and the people we admire never tried to be. A team is not your life done for you; it is keeping the one thing you are good at and handing off the rest without apology.

spots.title: Khaana khaya?
spots.director: The Humanist: Hinglish as spoken, fillers and all; two kitchens, one cut; the spoken word is handwriting, the written word is type; Keybot writes, she sends.
spots.job: Keybot: filler out, punctuation in, names kept; Hindi and Hinglish first.
spots.logline: A mother in Jaipur speaks to her phone the way she speaks, woh and all. Her son in Bengaluru, cooking alone at the same minute, reads it as she meant it.
spots.insight: Maa does not type: the keyboard is small, in the wrong script and slower than her mouth. Keybot lets her speak and hands her writing: her words, her names, her commas, the fillers brushed off like crumbs from a table. She presses send.

spots.title: Leave at 4:40
spots.director: The Minimalist: no screen ever shown; one line of type placed late; one event, a hard cut; the frames vast and the holds honest.
spots.job: Plan: your calendar and to-dos; when to leave.
spots.logline: A coat by a door, one small note taped to the frame, and a person who walks, not runs, to a train that arrives as she reaches it.
spots.insight: Being on time is not a skill, it is a quiet mind. Plan does one unglamorous thing here, it tells you when to leave, and we show what that buys: a walk.

spots.title: The Hold
spots.director: The Precisionist (Fincher): the camera never gets excited, the cut does; a clock under everything; tension held one beat past comfort and released by the smallest sound.
spots.job: Travel, and the value: it finds, you always press pay.
spots.logline: A sprinter, a chess hand, a train, a diver, all held a frame before they go. A bot finds the whole trip and then waits, looking at you, until a hand writes yes.
spots.insight: Trust is built by watching something that could act, and doesn't. The most expensive second in anyone's day is the one before 'pay'. If a bot can hold that second with everything ready and nothing taken, it can be trusted with the rest.

spots.why_cinema: Built to be mute: four things ready that do not go, four cards, a question, a button, and a creature that looks at the button and then at you and does not touch it. Then a hand writes yes, a stamp says Paid, and the whole held world moves at once.

spots.title: Go Live
spots.director: The Precisionist, second film, its own shape: it opens on the hands, not on black; two holds, not four; the room stands before the rocket goes; one slam. It shares with The Hold only the wait, the written yes and the stamp.
spots.job: Code bot: a safe copy, tests, asks when it needs you; nothing goes live till you say yes. The computer platform seen.
spots.logline: Hands lift off a keyboard at night and a clock starts. A rocket sits venting on its pad. The bot has done the work on a copy, proved it, and waits for one handwritten yes; then a room stands up and the rocket goes.
spots.insight: The fear of letting software ship is the fear of a thing acting while you look away. A bot that does the dangerous part on a copy, proves it, and then holds at T-minus until you say go is a bot you can hand the keys to.

spots.title: In One Sentence
spots.director: The Symmetrist's paper and the Trickster's hands: a sentence becomes a creature, the creature takes the centre seat, the row is now five.
spots.job: Make your own bot; the team grows.
spots.logline: Running shoes by a door at night. A woman says what she wishes someone would do for her, in one sentence. On paper a new head draws itself, takes the empty centre seat beside the team, and leaves her a note for the morning.
spots.insight: The bot people most want is the one nobody built for them. Asking for it should cost one plain sentence, and getting it should feel like a new face at the table, not a form.

spots.title: Uncle is right
spots.director: The Humanist: the family's sceptic uncle, a dubbed-interview look Indian viewers know, and a brand that stops the film to agree with him.
spots.job: Value, India: you stay in charge; you always press pay. The fox's first appearance.
spots.logline: A retired professor who happens to be a fox says the one thing every Indian family's sceptic says about machines and money. The brand stops the film and agrees with him on paper.
spots.insight: Every Indian family has an uncle who trusts no machine with money, and he has usually been right. Trust is won by leaving your hand on the wallet. 'You always press pay' is that uncle's rule made into a product, and the most honest thing to say to him is: sahi hai.

spots.why_cinema: A talking head stopped mid-gesture, a bot nodding in agreement with the sceptic, a ticket with a button marked for his hand only; then the film warms because he said yes. He wins, and the brand is the one agreeing.

spots.title: The Witness
spots.director: The Precisionist: a deposition. Questions as type on black, answers as handwriting under a witness; the clock never stops until the end card.
spots.job: Trust, global: what X0 Bot is, defined by what it refuses to do (they ask first; data not for sale). The fox's second appearance.
spots.logline: A fox is cross-examined about his bots. He answers in as few words as possible and wins the room with what they will not do.
spots.insight: Nobody believes a brand describing itself; everybody leans in when someone answers for it under pressure. The real fear about bots is not that they fail but that they act, so the product is best introduced by a witness who lists what it does and then, under hostile questioning, what it did without him: nothing.

spots.why_cinema: A text film disguised as a talking head: every question is type on black, every answer is handwriting under a creature who has nothing to hide, the team assembles in colour as he names it, and the lone 'No.' held in a freeze is the hinge a thumb stops on. Then the warmth drains out of him and the type lands.

system: FORMAT: 9:16, 1080x1920, 30 fps; every spot ends on the fixed 4.5 s end card counted inside its length; every spot reads with the sound off from frame one (something moves or writes within the first 0.8 s). SAFE AREA: all type sits between 0.12h and 0.80h and left of 0.88w; headline baseline no lower than 0.78h; small lines go ABOVE the headline or beside a card, never below 0.80h; timestamps and timecodes at 0.12h; Q cards left-aligned at 0.08w. TYPE: headlines in heavy Geist (Geist Black), two lines, no full stop, one word in Caveat, one brush underline in the bot's own colour (Keybot clay #A9573A, Plan ochre #8F6A1F, Travel sea #3E6E8E, Code bot moss #4F7A3A) or the icon's clay #C9683F when no single bot owns the film; ink #0A0A0A on paper, white on footage. HEADLINE LENGTH: a line of up to 12 characters sets at 0.09w cap height; 13-14 characters at 0.08-0.085w; 15 characters only as a named exception at 0.075w (Khaana khaya?); nothing longer is written. Builders set the real font and measure every line against 1026 px (a 2.5% margin each side) before paper is drawn. Small lines in Geist regular 0.03-0.035w, grey on paper, white on footage; 0.035w is the floor for any line that carries a claim, and those lines are ink, not grey. LUMINANCE: measure the band behind any white type; above 60% grey, add a 40% ink gradient or a letterbox bar behind it, or move the type to the dark side of the frame. GRAMMAR: what a person SAYS is Caveat handwriting on the voice's word times with a pen scratch per word; unvoiced handwriting runs at 0.3 s per word with 0.5 s before a typed reply; what is SETTLED or what a bot DID is Geist type, typed with a tick per letter or slammed in one frame (scale 1.08 to 1.00 in 3 frames); a bot's card is never in Caveat except for the words a person told it. PAPER: white cotton paper with faint grain; taped cards are white, one or two tape strips, the bot's dotted head top-left with its name in small Geist, text in ink Geist 0.045w; every card is sized to its longest line plus 0.04w padding (card text may drop to 0.035w, never below, and a long line breaks in two); drawn buttons are dip-pen outlines ('Pay' or 'Yes') always with a smaller 'Not now' beside them, and only a hand writes on one, only in The Hold and Go Live, where a hand-drawn stamp then lands ('Paid', 'Live'); the painted X0 mark is three brush strokes; the dip-pen hairline rule and the 36 px mount belong to the Symmetrist films. FREEZE: the freeze that goes cold (saturation down a third, two degrees cooler, grain up, pulse out, over 6 frames) marks a problem or a pause; a freeze that stays warm marks agreement (Pahunch gaye, Uncle is right). GRADE: all footage in a spot shares one grade (contrast up, saturation -25 to -40%, fine grain, soft vignette); archive keeps its scratches and flicker and is graded to brand greys, never sepia; the Precisionist pair is cold and the fox deposition crushes blacks to ink. ARCHIVE AND MARKS: public-domain archive carries insignia (NASA, telephone companies, railroads); punch in 110-120%, mask or grade out lettering, choose frames without insignia, and flag any clip that cannot be cleared before cutting; phone, shoe and vehicle logos and railway liveries are cropped or masked. THE HERO: drawn alive, flat painted black, cream gloves, two big cream eyes, faceted edges; he hangs from his clay bar or from the top edge of someone else's footage, blinks, looks, nods; he touches text in exactly two films (the sweep in Great at One Thing, the flick in Khaana khaya) and never touches a card with a button; he winks only in Great at One Thing and on the end card, and on the end card he looks and waits instead in The Hold, Go Live and The Witness. The bots are dotted heads in their colours; Notes is ink; a user's own bot is a pencil outline that fills ink and sits in the centre seat (Great at One Thing leaves it open, In One Sentence fills it). FOOTAGE REUSE: clip 1's cook is the campaign's recurring man (Hands full, Great at One Thing, Khaana khaya); never run Great at One Thing and Khaana khaya in the same placement; in The Witness, alternate punch-ins (100/108/115%) between consecutive uses of overlapping fox segments and never start a repeated gesture on the same frame. SOUND FAMILY: a synthesised drone in one key per spot; a pulse (a wall clock at 60 bpm in the Precisionist pair and both fox films, hats or rail joints at 96-120 bpm elsewhere, none in the Minimalist, the Humanist kitchen and In One Sentence); one bell per bot in its own note (clay, ochre, sea, moss, a low ink bell for Notes, a soft grey bell for a made bot); tape rip for every card, pen scratch per handwritten word, typewriter tick per typed letter, paper slide, boom on slams, riser into releases, stamp thunk with a sub hit, a brush swish for every underline; neural voices via edge-tts (en-IN Prabhat for the documentarian and the uncle, en-IN Neerja for mothers and the maker, en-GB Ryan for the witness; Devanagari fallbacks hi-IN Swara and hi-IN Madhur with matched word counts), never more than one voice per film, never a word from a questioner; every VO line is timed against its window (about 2.1 words per second at -15%, 2.4 at -5%, plus 0.3 s per full stop) before build. END CARD (fixed, 4.5 s): the white sheet slides up with a paper whoosh over whatever is on screen; the hero already on his bar at 0.42w, upper third; the X0 mark (0.5w) drawn in three strokes on three low taps at +0.5, +1.0, +1.5; 'Your team of bots' in Geist 0.07w; the hand-drawn stamp 'Coming soon / x0bot.com' (0.45w, rotated -6°, bottom right) thuds at +3.5; the final chord opens at +0.5 and sustains in the spot's key. CUT-DOWNS: 'Who Presses Pay' (15 s) from The Witness with the extra recorded Ryan line 'You do' and a white headline 'You do' / 'always' with a clay underline under 'always'; 'Face Down' (6 s) from the sourced phone-face-down shot into the end card. COPY RULES, enforced on every word above: no prices, no other companies' or apps' names, no 'best' or rankings, no exclamation marks, nothing the app does not do (Keybot writes and the user sends, Keybot does not translate or send; bots find and ask, you press pay; Code bot works on a safe copy and nothing goes live till you say yes; a made bot plans and reminds), short plain words; 'Not for sale' to be confirmed with counsel before build; Prof. Lomri is a painted character, not a person.
